open_issues.description: The grant includes a right to sublicense, but no separate sublicense-receipts royalty rate appears in the supplied passages. Whether sublicensee sales or sublicense income count as Net Sales is unclear ('directly or indirectly to unrelated third parties'). No sublicensing term was extracted.
Tier wording ('X% of Net Sales from $A up to $B') is read as marginal bands; the text does not use the word marginal or all-units. Tier 1 lower bound is not stated and tier 4 has no upper bound.

The Minimum Royalty table is flattened into separate passages. Section 4.3 says Licensee 'shall pay' it, but Sections 3.1 and 4.5 frame it as a condition for keeping exclusivity. It is unclear whether it is a floor on earned royalties or additional, and whether the 1st Agreement Year is calendar 2009. The schedule is recorded as minimum-royalty payments pending review.

Section 4.1 is subject to Section 4.13, which caps Royalties at $200,000 for an Agreement Year in which Licensor does not provide requested services. Whether Licensee requests services, and how the cap interacts with the Minimum Royalty, cannot be determined from the document.

Royalty-bearing Products include Other Products only while Licensee chooses to use the MamaMancini Marks on them. Product Appendices (descriptions, recipes, acceptance dates) are blank in the supplied text, so the actual royalty-bearing product set is not determinable.

Internal references appear inconsistent: Section 1.3 refers to Section 4.4 (payment of royalties), Books and Records and Trademark clauses are both numbered 6, and Section 13.3 refers to non-existent paragraph 14.1. Section numbering may be misaligned or sections omitted in the extracted text.
The post-termination sell-off period requires payment of 'a Royalty' without restating the rate or whether tier thresholds reset; presumed to follow Section 4.2.

Section 13.6 requires written signed amendments. Amendments to the Agreement were not checked and no amendment is identified in the supplied text; this historical SEC exhibit does not establish current operative terms.
